claims.claim_text: John D. Archbold's last documented civilian livelihood before wartime Navy and OSS service was ownership and agricultural production at Springfield Plantation in Dominica.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Clemson's finding aid says Archbold purchased Springfield in 1935 and began producing citrus before diversifying its crops over the following decades.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by Clemson's full-name biography, which also independently identifies his Navy and OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: ownership and agricultural production began in 1935 and continued across the wartime period, but the finding aid gives no exact Navy entry or separation date.
claims.match_notes: Springfield is labeled the last documented civilian livelihood, not an explicitly stated final employer. The self-employment relationship preserves the distinction between ownership and salaried employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Anthony A. Archuleta Jr. is the same Anthony A. Archuleta Jr. whose 1942 Army enlistment is transcribed from NARA records.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA index and enlistment transcription share the exact full indexed name, suffix, and a unique service identifier retained only in the private database; a cemetery transcription independently expands the middle name to Aaron.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact full name and suffix plus a unique private service-identifier match, with compatible World War II Army status and an independent middle-name expansion.
claims.temporal_assessment: The enlistment transcription places Army entry in 1942; the OSS index later records him as a Private First Class. The cemetery entry corroborates World War II Army service.
claims.match_notes: The service identifier is used only for private identity resolution and is excluded from claim text, excerpts, source metadata, and public downloads.

claims.claim_text: Anthony A. Archuleta Jr.'s best-supported immediate pathway into OSS was United States Army service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The enlistment transcription records Army entry from civilian life in 1942, and the NARA OSS index later records Archuleta as a Private First Class.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact full name and suffix plus a unique private service-identifier match shared by the index and enlistment transcription.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded military pathway: Army entry precedes the indexed OSS record, but no reviewed source names his unit or gives an exact OSS assignment date.
claims.match_notes: Civil Life is preserved as an enlistment-source category and is not converted into an employer or occupation. Army service is modeled as a military assignment.
